notes: Account background: Large regional insurer, heavy paper claim backlog + imaging, aggressive roadmap to automate first-pass claim decisions and agent assist.
Primary ask: evaluate Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower per-token unit economics vs public hosted; strict SLOs for customer-facing chat and agent assist flows.
Throughput targets: baseline 150 QPS for short chat/assist (avg 64 tokens), burst to 400 QPS for batch reranking windows (nightly prioritization).
Latency SLOs: target P95 <= 180ms for 0-512 token assistant responses; for longer summarization flows (2–8k tokens) acceptable up to P95 800–1200ms but want guidance on pipeline splitting.

Reserved GPU planning: preference for nodal pools sized around 8 x H100/H800 equivalent for production canaries; ask for throughput per-GPU numbers at 2k and 8k context. Need cost/throughput trade table.
Model preferences: fine-tuned open models (Llama-family variants) + vendor models for backstop. Must support quantized int8 profiles; interested in int4 if quality holds for extraction tasks.
Model-specific tuning requests: recommended context length for claim doc summarization = 8k tokens; ask Redwood for kv-cache memory implications and eviction policy recommendations.

Batching/KV cache: want autoscaling + dynamic batching but strict tail-latency guarantees. Concerned about batching-induced latency spikes during low-concurrency spikes. Looking for continuous-batching options with max wait thresholds.

Quantization testing: ask for Redwood Optimize-run A/B of int8 vs int4 on named model set with evaluation on proprietary claim prompts. Put quality regressions tied to acceptance criteria (F1/ROUGE thresholds).

Security/compliance notes: SSO via SAML required, KMS integration for key rotation, audit logs retention requested for 7 years for certain data categories. VPC peering with existing prod network required (non-intrusive).
Quote from CTO (02/04 workshop): 'We cannot tolerate >200ms P95 for live agent-facing responses — anything slower increases call handling time and CX risk.'
Quote from Legal: 'Data residency clauses must be explicit; EU customer dossiers cannot leave EU processing region.'

POC scope agreed: 3-week performance POC using Redwood Dedicated staging pool. Run workload mix: 60% chat/agent assist, 30% doc summarization (multi-doc), 10% reranking. Deliverables: perf matrix, SLA draft, quantization quality report.
Driving factors: predictable unit cost, demonstrable latency SLOs, full auditability, and contract-level uptime SLA for critical inference endpoints.
Internal champion: Head of Automation — wants pilot in Q2; Procurement and Legal are gating factors.
Redwood asks: full sample prompt set (anonymized), representative token length distribution, latency budget per route, baseline QPS curves, and a list of EU-resident datasets to plan residency.
Red flags: wants fallback behavior documented (e.g., degrade to smaller model with identical API) and precise routing policy for model variants during capacity constraints.
